post.title: How your student loan charges interest on interest
post.ig:
Your student loan can charge interest on its own interest.

It's called capitalization: unpaid interest is added to your principal.
New undergrad federal loans (July 2026 to June 2027) carry a fixed 6.52%.
Example: $10,000 unpaid for 4 years builds $2,608 in interest. If it capitalizes, yearly interest goes from $652 to about $822.
Since July 2023, federal loans no longer capitalize when you enter repayment or leave forbearance, but consolidation, leaving IBR and some deferments still trigger it.

Sources: US Department of Education (Federal Register, Nov 2022; FSA, June 2026), studentaid.gov.

Capitalization adds unpaid interest to your student loan principal, so interest starts earning interest. New undergrad federal loans for July 2026 to June 2027 carry a fixed 6.52%; in a $10,000 example, capitalizing four years of unpaid interest raises yearly interest from $652 to about $822. Since July 2023, federal loans no longer capitalize when you enter repayment or leave forbearance, but consolidation, leaving IBR and some deferments still trigger it. Sources: US Department of Education (Federal Register, Nov 2022; FSA, June 2026), studentaid.gov.
